This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **184** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/package.json`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-credential-migration.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/package.json`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-credential-migration.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0647dabb06ee314981b25fcc5a15de304de42c9d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fbd7a7327dd6456a3195b239d4059700318a3827` — the merge of head `b512d18ad062ad576b3c34f9bf84a3cdddb220fd` into base `0647dabb06ee314981b25fcc5a15de304de42c9d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fbd7a7327dd6456a3195b239d4059700318a3827 && git checkout fbd7a7327dd6456a3195b239d4059700318a3827
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0647dabb06ee314981b25fcc5a15de304de42c9d b512d18ad062ad576b3c34f9bf84a3cdddb220fd && git checkout -B drift-repro 0647dabb06ee314981b25fcc5a15de304de42c9d && git merge --no-ff b512d18ad062ad576b3c34f9bf84a3cdddb220fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0647dabb06ee314981b25fcc5a15de304de42c9d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0647dabb06ee314981b25fcc5a15de304de42c9d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read at the head with `git show` / `git diff origin/main...ff6ed731`; the card (#31328) body and all six comments; the PR body; the 70 check-runs on the head (every one `success` or a declared `skipped`; none failed).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the tree:

1. **New driver id `oracle`, alias `oracledb`** — `DRIVER_VOCABULARY` gains a row with `aliases: []`, `contractOnlyAliases: ['oracle', 'oracledb']`, `federationOnly: true`, `hasLocalDefault: false`. `resolveDriverId('oracle' | 'oracledb' | ' OracleDB ')` → `'oracle'`; `resolveDatabaseDriverId` → `undefined` for both spellings; `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_ALIASES` and `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` unchanged in content; `BUILTIN_DRIVER_IDS` gains `oracle` at the end (tuple order kept). Both boot hosts (`packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`) resolve through the selection face, so neither can select Oracle as the platform store; the CLI parity test pins the refusal in dev and prod. **Right** — it is the memory row's established "contract face yes, selection face no" shape, reused for a second reason, and the config-registry docblock says so.
2. **`DriverType` accepts `'oracle'`** — `DriverType` is `z.string()` with regex refusals for retired spellings only, so the new spelling needs no change there; `DatasourceSchema.safeParse({ driver: 'oracle', schemaMode: 'external', external, config })` succeeds (pinned). **Right.**
3. **Federation-only refusal on a managed datasource** — `datasource.zod.ts` superRefine: `ds.schemaMode === 'managed' && isFederationOnlyDriver(ds.driver)` → issue at path `schemaMode`. `schemaMode` defaults to `'managed'`, so a datasource that names the driver and nothing else is refused (pinned for both spellings); `'external'` and `'validate-only'` are accepted (pinned). The gate that enforces the same rule at the driver, `ClassHeadFacet.assertDialectEmits`, refuses every DDL operation on `ORACLE_CLIENTS` with `UnsupportedDialectEmissionError(..., 'federation-only')` before the Postgres-wire check; the factory arm connects only. Rule and gate agree. **Right.**
4. **Oracle `ssl` block refusal** — a datasource-level `ssl` block on `driver: oracle` is refused at path `ssl` when `enabled === true`, `rejectUnauthorized === false`, or any of `ca` / `cert` / `key` is set; the block's own defaults (`enabled: false`, `rejectUnauthorized: true`, read off the parsed value) pass, and `ssl: { enabled: false }` is pinned accepted. `OracleConfigSchema` refuses `ssl` / `ca` / `cert` / `key` / `rejectUnauthorized` inside `config` by name. The factory's `assertOracleSslNotDeclared` applies the same predicate at the last door for stored rows. **Right as a refusal** (refusing beats dropping); the prose it carries is a should-fix (④.4).
5. **`OracleConfigSchema`** — `connectString` (placeholder-free, supersedes the discrete keys) or `host` + `serviceName`, `port` default `1521`, `username` optional, `password` a `refusedInlineCredentialKey`; superRefine requires a connection target; `url` / `sid` / `autoMigrate` / `pool` / `schemaMode` / `readOnly` / `passwd` / `pwd` refused with guidance; aliases `hostname`/`server`→`host`, `service`/`service_name`/`database`/`dbname`→`serviceName`, `connect_string`/`connectionstring`/`tns`/`dsn`→`connectString`, `user`→`username`. Matches the postgres shape (url-supersedes-host, optional username, refused inline password) minus the local default, which is right for `hasLocalDefault: false`. The factory reads exactly these keys (`connectString` verbatim, else `host:port/serviceName`, password = bound secret). JSON-Schema projection and `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` row (`""`, `connectString`, `host`, `serviceName`, `username`) follow the postgres pattern. **Right.**
6. **New exports** — `OracleConfigSchema`, `OracleConfig`, `OracleConfigParsed`, `getOracleConfigJsonSchema`, `ORACLE_DEFAULT_PORT`, `FEDERATION_ONLY_DRIVER_IDS`, `isFederationOnlyDriver`, `FederationOnlyDriverId`, `DatabaseSelectionDriverId` = the nine additions in `api-surface/data.json`; `driver/index.ts` re-exports `oracle.zod`. **Right**, with one caveat: `resolveDatabaseDriverId`'s return type and `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS`'s element type narrow from `BuiltinDriverId` to `DatabaseSelectionDriverId`. Runtime values are unchanged; the type narrowing is a fact of the table (no selection alias resolves to a federation-only id) and is pinned. It is invisible to the api-surface ratchet (names only), and two in-repo consumers (`config-registry.test.ts`, `driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts`) needed `as readonly string[]` casts to keep compiling — see ②.
7. **`SqlDialect` gains `'oracle'`; `DIALECT_ALIASES.oracle`** — `varchar2`, `nvarchar2`, `char`, `nchar`, `clob`, `nclob`, `long`, `rowid`, `urowid` → text; `number` → decimal (bare); `float`, `binary_float`, `binary_double` → float; `date`, `timestamp`, `timestamp with local time zone` → datetime (`… with time zone` reaches `timestamp` through the existing suffix strip; `timestamp(6) with local time zone` through the paren strip — both pinned); `raw`, `long raw`, `blob`, `bfile` → binary; `boolean` → boolean; `json` → json. Every type the card lists is covered. **Right.**
8. **`NUMBER(p,s)` / `RAW(n)` read before the parameter strip** — `oracleParameterisedType`: a positive scale → decimal; a zero or negative scale → integer when `p − s` is at most 9 digits, else bigint; `NUMBER(*,0)` (Oracle's `INTEGER`) → bigint; bare `NUMBER` → decimal; unreadable parameters (`NUMBER(x)`) → `undefined` → the bare-NUMBER answer; `RAW(16)` → uuid, other widths → binary; any other base returns `undefined` so `TIMESTAMP(6)`, `FLOAT(126)`, `INTERVAL DAY(2) TO SECOND(6)` take the generic path. The introspection arm (`oracleColumnTypeString`) spells exactly these strings from `DATA_PRECISION` / `DATA_SCALE` / `DATA_LENGTH` (`NUMBER`, `NUMBER(*,s)`, `NUMBER(p,s)`, `RAW(n)`), so producer and matrix agree by construction. The first consumer, `external-datasource-service.ts`, passes the driver's `dialectName` (`'oracle'` from `ManagedDriftFacet.dialectName`) straight through `typeVocabulary`. **Right.**
9. **The boolean judgment** — `NUMBER(1)` → integer → `boolean` is `'lossy'` (the shared `integer` row), `CHAR(1)` → text → `boolean` is `false`, native `BOOLEAN` → `true`; all three pinned. The driver then presents a *declared* boolean over `NUMBER(1)` as true/false on read (`readPresentationKind` / `formatOutput`) and binds a boolean as 1/0 (`prepBindings`, pinned) — a declared field type, not a silent coercion, and `CHAR(1)` never reaches it because Gate 2 refuses the pairing. **Right**, and it is what the card asked for.
10. **`DATE` → datetime** — a `date` field over it is `'lossy'`, a `datetime` field exact (pinned); without the dialect the same spelling is still `date`. **Right.**
11. **Metadata-protocol `added`** — a new accepted driver id and a new `config` contract (six authorable keys, `password` retired) widen what a metadata document may say; nothing is narrowed or re-read. **Right.**
12. **`''`-is-NULL, `$empty`, JSON membership, upsert** — driver refusals (`INVALID_FILTER` withheld-subtree, `null_only` arm, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`/501), not spec accept-set changes; read as the cited code behind the card's constraints and found consistent with the docs. Not re-judged here beyond that.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31328-oracle-federation-dialect.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/driver-sql: minor`, `@objectstack/service-datasource: minor`. The spec is at 18.3.0; the diff adds a driver id, a config contract, nine exports and one `SqlDialect` member, removes nothing and changes no existing answer (`canonicalizeSqlType(x)` without a dialect is byte-identical; every other dialect's table is untouched). Minor is the right level.

Clause-②: `yes (widening)` — declared identically on the PR body and in the changeset; the card expected it; the claim's provisional `yes` is confirmed from the diff.
Metadata-protocol: `added` — PR body and changeset agree.

The second changeset, `31328-driver-sql-columnmap-keyed-paging.md` (`@objectstack/driver-sql: patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`), is the temporary e7935cd8 commit's; its declarations are right for what it does (an ORDER BY tie-breaker, no accept-set change) and it is slated to drop out when #31342 lands — see ③.

One semver gap, should-fix: the narrowing of two published TypeScript signatures (`resolveDatabaseDriverId(): DatabaseSelectionDriverId | undefined`, `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS: readonly DatabaseSelectionDriverId[]`) is not named in the changeset. Runtime is unchanged, so `minor` holds, but a consumer passing a `BuiltinDriverId` to `.includes()` stops compiling — two in-repo consumers did and were cast. Name it in the changeset body so an upgrading agent grepping the tombstoned symbol finds it.

### ③ Boundary flags

From the os-dev-report (comment 6717632414):

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (paged read of a federated object keyed through `columnMap`, carrier #31342): right carrier. **Escalated to the epic PM:** the PR carries e7935cd8 and its patch changeset until #31342 lands; if this PR merged first the fix would publish twice (two changelog sentences for one change). The PR body states it stays draft until the next main merge after #31342; that condition must hold before ready, and the PM should confirm the duplicate commit and changeset are gone at the final head.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (extra-surface files): every file named is covered by a claim amendment on the card, the last (05:16Z) covering the analytics test and the parity test's `driver-turso` import. Answered.
- `dogfood_battery: n/a` — no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm. Right.
- Gates: "every check-run concluded success or an expected skip" — confirmed against the 70 check-runs on `ff6ed731`; the `check:test-typecheck` OOM the PR body mentions is not a gate verdict (the Type Check lanes are green).

From the PR body's known limitations:

- DST spring-forward gap in a non-UTC process: documented remedy `TZ=UTC`; a driver concern, no spec claim depends on it. Answered.
- `NUMBER` above 2^53 loses precision: the same bound every dialect's `bigint` carries; the type-compat docblock says so. Answered.
- Filtering or writing a `RAW(16)` column by its uuid string is unsupported: this contradicts the matrix's exact `lookup` over `RAW(16)` — should-fix ④.3.
- Introspection lists the current schema only; another owner's table via `remoteName: 'OWNER.TABLE'`: the same scope rule the other three arms follow; the `IS_LOCAL` / `referencedSchema` handling keeps cross-schema FK parents honest. Answered.
- Oracle not yet in the Studio driver-catalog connection form: the card's Task names the Tables tab and `list_remote_tables` / `import_object`, which read the introspection seam this PR provides; the connection form is an `../objectui` surface. **Escalated to the epic PM** as a follow-up card there (the card's "Studio" wording covers both readings; the epic's scenario needs the form before a maintainer can add an Oracle datasource without authoring code).

Card constraints:

- Live cell env: card said `ORACLE_URL`; claim amendment 2 set `OS_TEST_ORACLE_URL`; the tree uses `OS_TEST_ORACLE_URL` with `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_ORACLE=1`. Answered.
- Minimum version: Oracle 12c Release 1, stated in the dialect module and the docs. Answered (the ADR amendment is dialect-list only, so it need not restate it).
- Serial with #31327 (SQL Server): the vocabulary generalises by addition (`federationOnly?: true`, `FEDERATION_ONLY_DRIVER_IDS`, `isFederationOnlyDriver`, `federationOnlyDriverOnManagedRefusal(driverId)` parameterised; the `ssl` refusal is `=== 'oracle'` on purpose, since tedious does read TLS options). **For the reconciler of whichever PR lands second**, the hard-coded singletons that must widen: `config-registry.test.ts` (`withheld` equals `['memory', 'oracle']`; `FEDERATION_ONLY_DRIVER_IDS` equals `['oracle']`; the `BUILTIN_DRIVER_IDS` tuple), `driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` (`FEDERATION_ONLY_SPELLINGS`), the `federationOnly` docblock naming `oracle` alone, and the ADR §4.6 sentence "the one dialect whose type PARAMETERS change the answer".

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file, judged against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against (a legacy ERP/HIS estate on Oracle, read live, written behind both opt-ins, never managed).

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver/config-registry.zod.ts`** — against ADR-0015 §4.6 and its first consumers (`datasource.zod.ts`, the two boot hosts, the factory). The `federationOnly` column derives both faces (authoring refusal, selection withdrawal) from the one table rather than hand-listing at a consumer, which is the file's own rule and the right generalisation for #31327. `isFederationOnlyDriver` follows every alias face via `resolveDriverId` and answers `false` for plugin ids and non-strings (pinned). Holds. Should-fix ④.1: the `DatabaseSelectionDriverId` narrowing of two published signatures is undeclared (②).

**`packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts`** — against the ADR's Gate 1 and the driver's `assertDialectEmits`. The refusal fires on the default mode, at the key whose value fixes it, and prescribes the mode and the `external` block; an author following it lands on the accepted shape in one edit. The `ssl` refusal reads the parsed block, so defaults pass and only a key that asks for or shapes TLS is refused. Holds. Should-fix ④.2: `federationOnlyDriverOnManagedRefusal` ends "use a driver that can be managed (postgres, mysql or sqlite)" — a hand-written list that omits `turso`, `sqlite-wasm` and `mongodb`, in the module whose sibling refusals and the registry's own docblock say the selection face is derived, never hand-listed; derive it from `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS`.

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver/oracle.zod.ts`** — against the factory arm and the postgres contract it mirrors. Every key is read by `buildOracleConnection`; every refused key names the spelling that works; the connection-target refinement is the postgres one with no local default. Tried to break: `connectString` + `host` both set silently prefers `connectString` — the postgres `url` does the same, by documented contract; `tns: 'ERPDB'` becomes `connectString: 'ERPDB'`, which Thin resolves through `tnsnames.ora` — fine. Holds.
